 Home / Finance / Personal Finance / 3% DA hike: How much will your monthly salary rise? Check calculations 3% DA hike: How much will your monthly salary rise? Check calculations
 Centre's revision is expected to raise DA from 60% to 63% of basic pay, with arrears payable from July 1, 2026.
 salary, money
 Amit Kumar New Delhi 3 min read Last Updated : Oct 29 2026 | 1:19 PM IST Listen to This Article
 A 3-percentage-point increase in dearness allowance (DA) will raise the monthly salary component of central government employees by an amount equal to 3 per cent of their basic pay. For an employee drawing basic pay of Rs 18,000, this translates into an additional Rs 540 a month, while someone with basic pay of Rs 50,000 will receive Rs 1,500 more.   The revision, announced on October 28, increases dearness relief (DR) for central government pensioners. The decision is expected to benefit 4.8 million employees and 6.8 million pensioners, according to a report by Mint.   The revised DA rate is expected to rise from 60 per cent to 63 per cent of basic pay. The actual increase in take-home salary, however, will depend on applicable deductions and other salary components.     How much will your salary increase after the 3 per cent DA hike?
   The additional DA is calculated on basic pay, not on the total salary or the existing DA amount. Employees with higher basic pay will therefore receive a larger increase in rupee terms.   The following calculations assume that the existing DA rate is 60 per cent and the revised rate is 63 per cent.  Rs 56,100 Rs 33,660 Rs 35,343 Rs 1,683

 Rs 1,00,000 Rs 60,000 Rs 63,000 Rs 3,000 
 These figures represent the additional DA before deductions. They do not indicate an equivalent increase in the employee's entire take-home salary.   How is the DA hike calculated?
   Under the 7th Central Pay Commission (CPC) pay structure, DA is calculated as a percentage of basic pay.   The formula is:   Additional monthly DA = Basic pay × 3 ÷ 100   For an employee drawing basic pay of Rs 35,000, the calculation would be as follows:   Basic pay: Rs 35,000   Existing DA at 60 per cent: Rs 21,000   Revised DA at 63 per cent: Rs 22,050   Additional monthly DA: Rs 1,050   Additional DA over 12 months: Rs 12,600, assuming the rate remains unchanged throughout the period.   The increase applies to the DA component alone. House rent allowance (HRA), transport allowance and other salary components are separate. Employees should not calculate the 3 per cent increase on their gross salary, as this would overstate the benefit.   Will employees receive DA arrears from July 2026?
   The revised rate is effective from July 1, 2026. Eligible employees are therefore entitled to arrears for the period between the effective date and the implementation of the revised payment, subject to the government's payment arrangements.   For example, an employee with basic pay of Rs 18,000 would be entitled to an additional Rs 540 for every eligible month.   If four months of arrears are payable, the amount would be Rs 2,160. An employee with basic pay of Rs 50,000 would receive Rs 6,000 for the same four-month period.   The final arrears will depend on the number of eligible months and the official implementation and payment schedule. Employees should check the relevant government order or their department's salary communication for confirmation of the amount and payment date.     More From This Section
